title: Introduce temporal consensus evaluator and recourse gate
author: Aditi Rao
release_notes: Add a temporal consensus evaluator which aggregates signal across windows and surfaces actionable recourse suggestions; introduces a CI gate that transitions failing regressions into a prioritized recourse queue instead of hard-blocking merges by default.
description:
Motivation and summary: We observed noisy transient regressions in prompt-set checks where short-lived fluctuations would cause hard CI failures and frequent revert loops. This PR implements a Temporal Consensus Evaluator (TCE) that smooths evaluation signals across sliding windows and a Recourse Gate that offers suggested remediation steps (recourse) for failing prompt cohorts. The goal is to reduce merge noise while making regressions actionable: instead of immediate hard-blocks, the gate can (configurable) queue items for triage, annotate PRs with suggested fixes, and escalate sustained failures.

What this PR contains (single-string summary including commits, files, and conversations):
- High-level changes: add tce core logic, windowed aggregator, consensus policy engine, recourse suggestion generator, a CI adapter that integrates with the existing eval CI runner, and dashboards/telemetry hooks for surfaceability.
- Commits (summary):
  * 1a2b3c4: feat(tce): initial temporal consensus evaluator and aggregation primitives (core algorithm + tests)
  * 2b3c4d5: feat(recourse): recourse suggestion generator and suggestion templating (yaml-driven)
  * 3c4d5e6: feat(ci): integrate TCE with eval CI; add gate adapter + soft-fail fallback
  * 4d5e6f7: docs: add runbook and playbook for triage + sample recourse templates
  * 5e6f7g8: infra: add dashboard queries and telemetry counters + e2e smoke tests

- Files changed (high level):
  * eval_harness/tce/core.py (+230/ +20) -- aggregator, windowing, consensus rule set. Important function: compute_consensus(windowed_results: List[float], quorum: float) -> (bool, float) (code simplified in PR for review).
  * eval_harness/tce/policy.py (+120/ +8) -- consensus policy DSL, thresholds, TTL semantics for transient events.
  * eval_harness/recourse/generator.py (+90/ +10) -- suggestion templating engine (yaml-backed), link generation for reproducible runs.
  * ci/adapters/eval_tce_adapter.py (+80/ +15) -- adapter that hooks into eval CI run, posts annotations to GitHub, and optionally queues recourse items to the triage service.
  * tests/tce/test_consensus.py (+60/ +5) -- unit tests covering edge cases (outliers, missing windows, partial coverage).
  * docs/runbooks/tce-triage.md (+45/ +0) -- operator guide and sample playbook for recourse handling.
  * dashboards/tce_metrics.sql (+25/ +0) -- dashboard query templates used by the Console.
  * smoke/eval_tce_smoke.py (+10/ +84) -- e2e smoke harness used by CI to validate gate behavior.

- Small illustrative snippet (in description only, not a diff file):
  compute_consensus:
    window_scores = [0.82, 0.78, 0.81, 0.44, 0.79]
    # policy: quorum=0.6, sustained=3 -> majority of recent windows must exceed threshold
    result = compute_consensus(window_scores, quorum=0.6, sustain=3)  # returns (True, 0.8)

Design notes and rationale:
- Temporal smoothing: TCE keeps an exponentially-weighted sliding window and supports both count-based and time-based windows to accommodate backfilled runs. This addresses flaky, single-run regressions while still catching sustained degradations.
- Consensus policy: policy DSL allows per-prompt-set rules: quorum, sustain, decay, and quarantine duration. Default policy is conservative: soft-fail -> recourse queue. Enterprise customers can opt for stricter behaviour via config.
- Recourse: suggestions are generated from a small rulebase + nearest-failure-exemplar search. Suggestions include: reverting recent prompt edits, running deterministic seeds, increasing beam/temperature, or pinning model variant. Suggestions are surfaced as annotated checklist items in the PR.
- Observability: added counters for windows evaluated, consensus triggers, recourse suggestions emitted, and triage queue latency. Dashboards included for quick inspection.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for aggregator and policy DSL.
- Smoke e2e runs were flaky in first CI run due to race in the triage queue client; fixed by adding idempotent enqueue and improving backoff handling (commit 5e6f7g8).
- CI status: initial pipeline failed on smoke tests (intermittent) on 2026-02-18; after fix, full CI passed on 2026-02-22. All checks green at merge time.

Review conversation (selected excerpts, chronological):
- Miguel Vargas (reviewer): "Nice approach. Two asks: (1) can we expose per-prompt TTL in the policy, (2) add a small integration test that simulates backfilled runs so we don't mis-classify old regressions as new?"
- Aditi Rao (author): "Added TTL parameter to policy DSL and a backfill simulation test (tests/tce/test_backfill_sim.py) in follow-up commit. Backfill test simulates delayed runs and validates that decay semantics are correct."
- Claire Huang (reviewer): "What's the operational story for recourse suggestions turning noisy? We should ensure a human-in-the-loop threshold before auto-enqueue escalations."
- Aditi Rao: "Default is human-in-the-loop. The recourse_queue has a 'ready_for_autoresolve' flag; that requires admin opt-in. Documented in docs/runbooks/tce-triage.md."
- Samir Patel (approver): "Approvals pending green CI and a short runbook update. Once CI is green, I'm fine with squash-merge."

Edge cases and constraints called out:
- Consistency vs latency: smoothing introduces detection lag; policy sustain values are tunable per prompt-set.
- Storage: TCE persists compact window summaries (not raw traces) to keep storage bounded. Large backfills will create more load; we added a janitor to cap retention.
- Security: recourse links do not contain sensitive inputs; suggestions reference anonymized run IDs.

Operational runbook highlights (docs/runbooks/tce-triage.md excerpt summarized):
- How to triage a recourse item: reproduce with pinned model + seed, run smoke harness, annotate PR with reproduction trace.
- When to escalate: a recourse item that fails policy for 3 consecutive days auto-adds to the high-priority queue (requires admin opt-in).
- Rollback behavior: gate supports a manual 'force-pass' for emergency fixes with audit logs.

Why this is different from previous eval gates:
- Previous gates were single-run threshold checks. TCE reasons across time, making it better at distinguishing transient noise from regression trends while still surfacing actionable remediation. The recourse mechanism aims to convert noise into triageable work instead of merge friction.

Follow-ups (planned):
- Add server-side summary caching to reduce evaluation cost for large prompt-sets.
- Add an ML-based recourse ranker to prioritize suggestions generated by the rulebase.
- Expose per-customer policy templates in the Console for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Merge outcome and method: Squash-merged after CI green and final approvals. Merge commit message summarized key points and linked Linear tasks ENG-4871 and ENG-4902.

Notes on uniqueness: This PR intentionally emphasizes an operator-centric recourse flow and temporal consensus rather than only stricter CI gates; it is intended to reduce merge churn while improving signal-to-noise for prompt-set regressions.
